C08-M03-L01-F1.title: Inside the SIEM ingestion layer: six filing decisions
C08-M03-L01-F1.caption: The ordered stages between an event's arrival at the SIEM and the moment it becomes searchable, each with its typical silent failure.
C08-M03-L01-F1.alt: Flow diagram, top to bottom. Receive (input: port, endpoint, agent, API; failure: wrong input defaults). Break into events (line, multi-line, size limit; failure: split or merged events). Label source + type (host, source, source type; failure: relay recorded as host). Assign time (event time + ingest time; failure: receipt time substituted). Route (index, tier, access, filter; failure: wrong index or dropped). Write + index (searchable after refresh; failure: indexing delay under load).
C08-M03-L01-F1.note: Delivered is not filed: each stage can mis-file evidence without raising an error.

C08-M03-L01-F2.title: minisiem load() versus production ingestion
C08-M03-L01-F2.caption: Behaviours observed when loading the Banyan dataset with the teaching SIEM, paired with what a production ingestion layer must do instead.
C08-M03-L01-F2.alt: Comparison of two columns. minisiem load() (teaching): one file, one line per event; source copied from the event; event time only, no ingest time; everything in one table; duplicates stored silently (341 vs 340); one bad line aborts the load, table left empty; raw kept beside 12 columns. Production ingestion: many inputs, per-source-type breaking rules; host, source and source type set and validated; event time plus ingest time recorded; routing by data type, retention and access; de-duplication or a duplicate-rate check; bad events quarantined, the rest ingested; raw kept beside parsed fields.
